entries.dateLabel: Revision July 2020. Registry listing dated 22 August 2020.
entries.title: Infant lifejackets on passenger voyages
entries.scope: Liberian passenger ships within the notice's SOLAS application. Voyage duration and the complement of children and infants matter.
entries.summary: Below 24 hours the infant-lifejacket allowance uses 2.5% of passengers. From 24 hours the notice specifies one per infant. It gives a separate minimum for children.

entries.dateLabel: Revision July 2020. Registry listing dated 22 August 2020.
entries.title: Cargo-ship immersion suits and safety-equipment surveys
entries.scope: Liberian cargo ships covered by the cited SOLAS provisions. Establish construction date, trade, ship type, survey date and remote watch stations.
entries.summary: Section 1.3 links carriage to the first safety-equipment survey on or after 1 July 2006. Section 1.2 addresses non-bulk ships trading exclusively within 32°N–32°S and retains specified survival-craft equipment.

entries.authority: Panama Maritime Authority, General Directorate of Merchant Marine
entries.dateLabel: Revised September 2023. Listed in the authority's valid circulars as of 31 October 2026.
entries.title: Small cargo ships on the international register
entries.scope: Panamanian cargo vessels with an international Registry Certificate. The notice uses gross register tonnage (GRT). Crew boats have a separate equivalency route.
entries.summary: The cited resolution covers cargo ships below 500 GRT. The exclusions include below 100 GRT, length under 24 metres, unpropelled vessels, non-trading pleasure yachts and fishing vessels. Section 4 addresses distance from shore and an exemption certificate when specified survival craft are absent.

entries.authority: Panama Maritime Authority, General Directorate of Merchant Marine
entries.dateLabel: Issued June 2021. Listed in the authority's valid circulars as of 31 October 2026.
entries.title: Marine evacuation system servicing and deployments
entries.scope: Panamanian vessels fitted with a marine evacuation system. Verify the installation and any extension issued by the authority.
entries.summary: The notice gives a 12-month servicing interval, a possible authority extension to 17 months and a six-year maximum between rotational deployments. Keep the service and deployment history aboard.

entries.authority: Republic of the Marshall Islands Maritime Administrator
entries.dateLabel: November 2026 revision, retrieved on 23 November. It supersedes the December 2025 revision.
entries.title: Inspection and renewal of survival-craft launching falls
entries.scope: Marshall Islands SOLAS ships and mobile offshore units. The applicability clause also names commercial yachts and yachts engaged in trade at 500 GT or more, passenger yachts and private yachts limited charter under the Yacht Code.
entries.summary: The equipment section requires periodic inspection, particularly at sheaves. Deteriorating falls must be replaced when needed and the maximum renewal interval is five years.

entries.authority: Republic of the Marshall Islands Maritime Administrator
entries.dateLabel: September 2026 revision. It changes the lifebuoy table from the May 2022 edition.
entries.title: Lifebuoys on private yachts
entries.scope: Marshall Islands private yachts. Exclusions cover limited charter, yachts engaged in trade, and yachts holding the stated SOLAS or Yacht Code voluntary compliance statements.
entries.summary: The revised table specifies two lifebuoys below 24 m, four for yachts at least 24 m and below 500 GT, and eight in the 500 GT and above row. Use the table for position, lights, smoke signals and lines.

entries.authority: Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore
entries.dateLabel: Issued 20 November 2019. Paragraphs 1 and 6 apply the servicing standards from 1 January 2020. MPA Circular 2/2023 paragraph 4 defines active website circulars.
entries.title: Approval of lifeboat and rescue-boat servicing providers
entries.provision: Paragraphs 1–3 and 5–6, Annex question 7, pages 1–2 and 4
entries.scope: Singapore-registered ships with the lifeboats, rescue boats, launching appliances or release gear listed in paragraph 3.
entries.summary: MPA authorises its recognised organisations to approve providers. Annex question 7 explains the documented assessment and attending-surveyor arrangement when urgent work is needed and no approved provider is available in port.

entries.authority: Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore
entries.dateLabel: Issued 30 April 2026. Paragraph 8 changes eligibility of survey reports on 1 October 2026.
entries.title: Three-year pleasure-craft surveys and eligible surveyors
entries.scope: Singapore-registered pleasure craft intended for international voyages. Craft operating solely in the Port of Singapore follow the separate licensing regime described in paragraphs 3 and 5.
entries.summary: Surveys recur every three years. From 1 October 2026 MPA Port Inspector reports are no longer accepted. The circular specifies accredited surveyors and when a report must be submitted.

entries.authority: Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore
entries.dateLabel: Issued 30 April 2026. Paragraph 8 changes eligibility of survey reports on 1 October 2026.
entries.title: Construction, length and passenger limits for pleasure-craft registration
entries.scope: Applicants to the Singapore register for privately used pleasure craft going abroad. Check the owner and craft conditions and the application date.
entries.summary: Paragraph 6 specifies an enclosed deck, a minimum load-line length of seven metres, an age limit of 17 years at registration, hull restrictions and a maximum of 12 passengers. Paragraph 7(h) dates the survey report against the application.

entries.dateLabel: Issued and effective 20 November 2025. The authority posted the notice the next day.
entries.title: Immersion suits at remote cargo-ship watch stations
entries.scope: Bahamian cargo ships and mobile offshore units under paragraph 4. Check watch arrangements, bulk-carrier status, operating area and any exemption.
entries.summary: The notice gives minimum additional suits for bridge and machinery watches, including a smaller-ship exception for a sole engine-room watchkeeper. Section 6 gives the warm-climate limits and excludes bulk carriers from that exemption.

entries.dateLabel: Issued and effective 20 November 2025. The authority posted the notice the next day.
entries.title: Immersion suits and thermal protective aids on passenger ships
entries.scope: Bahamian passenger ships. Check lifeboat design, the rescue-boat or evacuation-system duties of the crew and any warm-climate determination.
entries.summary: Paragraph 5.2 specifies suits per lifeboat and thermal protection for other occupants. Paragraph 5.3 sets out the enclosed-lifeboat and warm-climate cases.

entries.dateLabel: Issued 30 October 2023. The notice gives 1 November 2023 as its effective date.
entries.title: Five-year lifeboat testing and authorised servicing
entries.scope: Bahamian ships fitted with the survival-craft launching appliances, on-load release gear or automatic release hooks named in section 2.
entries.summary: The notice separates routine inspections from servicing by authorised providers. It addresses dynamic load testing and the evidence for an exceptional short postponement requested through the recognised organisation.

coverage: Selected national notices from five flag administrations. Each reference identifies the exact passage in the publisher’s PDF. The profile conditions select research leads. Vessel classification, equipment, exceptions and later amendments require reading the cited source. Revision months are retained at their printed precision.
